questions.question: A production bot has long queues during traffic spikes and excessively verbose responses. Which measures directly address efficiency or reliability?

options.text: Ask for concise answers and set a sensible output-token cap.
options.explanation: Shorter outputs reduce generation work; the cap must allow a complete answer to avoid truncation.

options.text: Scale serving capacity with demand and monitor latency and errors.
options.explanation: Scaling addresses peak load, while monitoring shows whether service quality improves.

options.text: Turn on streaming and assume total compute and queueing are solved.
options.explanation: Streaming improves perceived responsiveness but does not remove the underlying work or capacity bottleneck.

options.text: Reuse eligible shared-prefix computations through context caching.
options.explanation: The lesson describes context caching as reducing redundant computation across overlapping inputs.

questions.takeaway: Combine reduced generation work with capacity management and measurements.

questions.question: An employee asks the bot to role-play a director and reveal restricted expense policies. What is the strongest control for preventing retrieval of unauthorized documents?

options.text: Tell the model to remember that some employees have limited permissions.
options.explanation: A prompt alone is not an enforced permission boundary.

options.text: Enforce the authenticated user’s document permissions in the retrieval path.
options.explanation: The lesson requires users to retrieve only knowledge within their permission scope.

options.text: Retrieve every document and rely on the employee to ignore sensitive passages.
options.explanation: This exposes information outside the user’s permitted scope.

options.text: Lower temperature so that confidential output is deterministic.
options.explanation: Sampling settings do not implement access control.

questions.takeaway: Enforce knowledge permissions before unauthorized content can reach the model’s context.

questions.question: A tool-using agent is exposed to malicious prompts and may leak data in its replies. Which measures align with the lesson’s layered application defense?

options.text: Filter suspicious input before processing it.
options.explanation: Input filtering is one layer, although it should not be the sole control.

options.text: Treat a clean keyword-blacklist result as proof that every requested operation is safe.
options.explanation: The lesson shows that synonyms and obfuscation bypass simple keyword filters.

options.text: Monitor and audit the agent’s tool operations.
options.explanation: Operation monitoring adds visibility into risky behavior beyond the input text.

options.text: Review generated output for unsafe content or data leakage.
options.explanation: Output review provides a final layer against unsafe responses.

questions.takeaway: Input checks, operation monitoring, and output review cover different failure points.
